title: Introduce presubmit fallback lanes and toolchain microimage bootstraps
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds deterministic lightweight presubmit fallback lanes and small toolchain microimages to reduce CI flakiness and iteration time. No breaking user-facing changes.
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline occasionally stalls or takes >30m for changes that only touch docs or small tooling. This PR introduces a lightweight fallback lane and microimage bootstraps so small changes still get fast, meaningful signal while preserving the full integration checks for code that touches runtime or infra.

Summary: Add a presubmit fallback runner that serializes and gates heavy integration steps behind a fastpath; introduce 'toolchain microimages' (slim bootstrap containers) to shrink cold-start time for ephemeral CI runners; wire a transparent reroute so that if the fastpath passes but heavy checks fail due to transient infra, the author gets actionable diagnostics and the heavy checks can be retried without blocking merges.

What changed (high level):
- New CI workflow: .github/workflows/presubmit-fallback.yml (fastpath + fallback orchestration)
- Toolchain microimages: devtools/toolchain/Dockerfile.micro and publish job in .github/workflows/build-toolchains.yml
- Lightweight runner script: ci/scripts/fallback-runner.sh (orchestrates fast checks, caches, and conditional enqueue of heavyweight lanes)
- Cache warmup helper: ci/tools/cache-warmup.go (small Go binary used in the microimage to populate common venv/node cache)
- Docs: docs/ci/presubmit.md (how to reason about the lanes and how to trigger full checks locally)
- Minor Makefile and devcontainer tweaks to support local dev parity

Commits (summary):
- a1f4d9b: initial presubmit fallback workflow + blueprint
- b2e5c3f: add Dockerfile.micro and build/publish job for microimages
- c3d8e1a: implement fallback-runner.sh; add unit tests for reroute logic
- d4f7f2b: cache-warmup tool and integration tests for microimage boot time
- e5b9010: docs and Makefile updates; add telemetry counters for fallback hits

Files changed (illustrative):
- .github/workflows/presubmit-fallback.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/build-toolchains.yml (modified)
- devtools/toolchain/Dockerfile.micro (new)
- ci/scripts/fallback-runner.sh (new)
- ci/tools/cache-warmup.go (new)
- docs/ci/presubmit.md (new)
- Makefile (tweaks)

Design notes / decisions:
- Fastpath checks include lint, unit tests, and quick static analysis; heavy lanes include integration tests and infra-sensitive smoke tests. A PR that only touches docs or small CLI utilities is routed to fastpath-only to preserve developer velocity.
- Microimages are intentionally minimal: pinned toolchain components + cache-warmup binary. The CI publishes these as immutable tags to reduce cold-start variability.
- Reroute behavior: when fastpath passes and heavy lane fails due to infra/timeouts, the PR is marked with a 'fallback: flaky-heavy' tag and maintainers are notified. Authors can opt to 'recheck heavy' via a comment command which re-queues the heavy lane; the fastpath result is retained (so reruns cost less).
- Telemetry: counters for fallback hits, requeue frequency, and microimage boot time were added to help tune thresholds.

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests for fallback-runner and cache-warmup (run under make test-fast).
- End-to-end smoke CI job in a feature branch that built/pulled the microimage and exercised the reroute path.
- Initial CI run: one flaky integration failure (external infra), fixed by a second re-run after retry logic was adjusted. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (abridged):
- Liam O'Connor (review): "Nice separation. Can we ensure the reroute metadata is idempotent and doesn't spam the PR comments? Also prefer a single env var to opt out for backcompat."
- Maya (author): "Addressed: added idempotent status marker and CI_OPT_OUT env var documented in presubmit.md. Split noisy logs behind DEBUG flag."
- Anika Singh (review): "Are images scanned by Snyk/Trivy as part of publish? We need a lightweight scan step."
- Maya: "Added a minimal Trivy scan in the publish job; it fails fast for high severity findings and is skipped for internal-only dev tags."
- Jordan Lee (approve): "Tests + docs look solid. Telemetry will help tune thresholds."

Edge cases and follow-ups:
- ENG-5189: Add automatic backoff for requeue attempts to avoid thrashing heavy lanes during infra incidents (tracked as follow-up).
- ENG-5240: Evaluate compressing existing larger toolchain images by extracting common layers (follow-up tech debt work).

Why this is different from previous work: Instead of only trimming CI matrices or splitting shards, this PR creates an orchestrated fastpath+fallback model that preserves strong signal without blocking developer flow, and pairs that with tiny, publishable microimages to reduce runtime variance. The combination reduces latency for small changes and improves CI reliability for larger runs.

Merge details: Squash-merged to main after CI green and three approvals.

Notes for maintainers:
- To tweak fastpath thresholds, see constants in ci/scripts/fallback-runner.sh and the presubmit workflow inputs.
- Microimages are published to demo-registry.redwood.internal (CI job name: build-toolchains/micro-publish). Access controlled by CI deploy key.

If you'd like a follow-up PR, I can:
- Add a devtooling script to let authors trigger local reproduction of the fallback path (ENG-5189)
- Expand telemetry dashboards in Redwood Console to include fallback lane KPIs

End of PR description.
